headline: AGNICO EAGLE Q2 RECORD: $1.6B NET INCOME, 855K oz AT $4,483 AVG — Record $625M Returned to Shareholders in a Single Quarter (NYSE/TSX: AEM)
snippet: Agnico Eagle Mines (TSX/NYSE: AEM) reported Q2 2026 results on July 29 that set company records across the board: net income of $1,600.5 million ($3.05 per diluted share, beating the $2.91 consensus estimate), 855,816 ounces produced at an average realized gold price of $4,483 per ounce, and record quarterly free cash flow driven by disciplined cost control. The company returned a record $625 million to shareholders through dividends and buybacks in a single quarter — a figure that underscores the extraordinary operating leverage available to high-quality gold producers at current gold prices. CEO Ammar Al-Joundi confirmed 'better-than-planned production' and reiterated commitment to long-term value creation, with the conference call held July 30 providing further detail on Finnish asset consolidation and growth project timelines.

headline: BRAZIL GOLD IPO: AMAPÁ MINERALS CLOSES $140M ON TSX — 1.5M-oz Past-Producer Recapitalizes at Guiana Shield, Joins Growing Canada IPO Rebound (TSX: AMAP)
snippet: Amapá Minerals Holdings Inc. (TSX: AMAP) closed its initial public offering on July 30, raising gross proceeds of $140 million through the sale of 127.27 million common shares at C$1.10 per share, with Canaccord Genuity and BMO Capital Markets as joint lead bookrunners and an overallotment option that could add another $21 million if exercised. The company's principal asset is the Amapá Project on Brazil's Guiana Shield — a past-producing open-pit gold operation that sold more than 1.5 million ounces of gold between 2005 and 2021 before being idled. The TSX listing contributes to what Mining.com is calling Canada's mining IPO rebound, as elevated gold prices and institutional risk appetite return capital to pre-production gold names at a pace not seen since 2020.

headline: SELKIRK COPPER MINTO MRE: 940M LBS Cu IN 47.8Mt — M&I Copper Up 182%, Gold Up 184% in Sweeping Yukon Resource Upgrade (TSXV: SCMI)
snippet: Selkirk Copper Mines Inc. (TSXV: SCMI) released an updated Mineral Resource Estimate on July 30 for its Minto Project in Yukon, reporting a Measured and Indicated Resource of 47.8 million tonnes at 0.89% copper — a 280% increase in total tonnage and 182% increase in M&I copper pounds compared to the 2025 estimate. Total contained metal stands at 940 million pounds copper, 530,000 ounces gold, and 4.97 million ounces silver. Gold grade is 0.34 g/t and silver 3.2 g/t, giving the project a meaningful polymetallic credit stack. The scale-up is driven by successful step-out and infill drilling programs that extended the orebody well beyond its previously modelled limits — the kind of resource growth narrative that historically re-rates junior copper developers when timed alongside a structural copper supply crunch.

headline: INDEPENDENCE GOLD BLIND VEIN #3: 2.8 g/t AU OVER 11.4m PLUS POLYMETALLIC ZONE — Dixie Discovery Expands 3Ts Epithermal District Near Artemis Blackwater, BC (TSXV: IGO)
snippet: Independence Gold Corp. (TSXV: IGO) announced July 30 the discovery of the Dixie Vein, a previously unknown blind epithermal system at its wholly owned 3Ts Gold and Silver Project in central British Columbia — the third blind vein discovery generated from the company's district-scale structural model, following Balrog and Goofy. Discovery hole 3TS-26-29 returned 11.40 metres grading 2.80 g/t gold and 12.54 g/t silver, including 1.99 metres of 6.94 g/t gold and 25.13 g/t silver, plus a lower polymetallic zone: 14.19 metres at 0.43% lead and 1.37% zinc. The 3Ts Project lies 16 km southwest of Artemis Gold's Blackwater Mine in the Nechako Plateau, and each new blind discovery confirms that the structural exploration model is reliably generating mineralized targets across the district.

headline: CAMBRIA GOLD PREMIER: 76.7 g/t AU CORE INSIDE 24.36 g/t OVER 6.3m — Prew Zone High-Grade Spine Confirmed at 12.5m Infill Spacing, BC (TSXV: CAMB)
snippet: Cambria Gold Mines Inc. (TSXV: CAMB) released July 28 additional assay results from underground infill drilling at the Prew Zone of the Premier-Northern Light deposit near Stewart, northwestern British Columbia, with hole P26U-0023 returning 6.3 metres averaging 24.36 g/t gold including 1.8 metres of 76.7 g/t gold. The 42-hole, 3,151-metre infill campaign is designed to tighten spacing to approximately 12.5 metres to define how the high-grade gold holds together at mineable scale. The Premier-Northern Light is a historically significant BC gold district, and infill results confirming a continuous 76 g/t core across a tight grid are exactly the data quality needed to underpin a resource conversion and eventual mine plan in a $4,000+ gold price environment.

headline: BANYAN GOLD NITRA MAIDEN DRILL: VISIBLE GOLD + 17.8 g/t AU AT ROARING FORK — Two New Zones Confirmed 25km West of AurMac Deposit, Yukon (TSXV: BYN)
snippet: Banyan Gold Corp. (TSXV: BYN) announced July 28 first results from the maiden drill program at its Nitra Gold Project in the Yukon — the first drilling ever conducted on the Nitra claims, located 25 km west of Banyan's flagship AurMac deposit. Discovery hole NT-26-001 at the Roaring Fork Zone intersected 1.62 g/t gold over 5.0 metres including a high-grade core of 17.80 g/t Au over 0.4 metres; separately, visible gold and mineralized quartz veins with bismuth-sulphosalts were logged in hole NT-26-006 at the Seattle Creek Zone. With assays pending from the lower half of NT-26-001 and most of the remaining 11 targets across 7,500 metres still to be tested, this opening result establishes mineralized zones in two blind targets simultaneously — a meaningful outcome for the first holes in a new district.

headline: BARKSDALE SAN JAVIER: 9m AT 3.464 g/t AU — AND 100% OWNERSHIP SECURED AFTER FINAL TUSK PAYMENT, Mexico (TSXV: BRO)
snippet: Barksdale Resources Corp. (TSXV: BRO) announced July 30 two concurrent milestones at its San Javier Gold Project in Mexico: drill results returning 9 metres at 3.464 g/t gold in hole SJ07-64 and 12 metres at 1.084 g/t gold from a resampling program, alongside completion of all payment obligations to Tusk, giving Barksdale 100% ownership of the project. Achieving 100% ownership eliminates ongoing payment obligations and vendor rights, simplifying the corporate structure at a time when the drill program is building a case for a resource estimate. For retail investors, the convergence of solid underground grades and clean 100% ownership in a $4,000 gold environment is the kind of structural improvement that precedes re-rating in small-cap gold explorers.

headline: HEDGE FUNDS DOUBLE DOWN: US ANTIMONY BORROW HITS 42%, RARE EARTH SHORTS SURGE — Grizzly Research and Peers Bet Political Tailwinds Can't Beat China's Supply Chain Lead
snippet: A July 30 Hedgeweek report using S&P Global Market Intelligence data reveals that hedge funds have sharply increased short positions against US critical minerals companies, with US Antimony Corporation's borrow rate jumping from 23% to 42% of market cap this year, American Resources Corporation rising from 9% to 23%, and bearish positioning climbing in MP Materials and USA Rare Earth. The bear case: developing new mines and processing capacity takes years and billions of dollars while China retains dominant control across mining, refining, and processing of rare earths and critical minerals — making current share prices a bet on a political agenda rather than operational cash flows. Grizzly Research is cited as one short-selling specialist arguing that 'some companies have benefited more from political momentum than underlying business performance.' This is the counternarrative investors should weigh against the 81% sector rally in H1 2026.

headline: CANADA MINING IPO REBOUND: GOLD MINERS CADILLAC AND AMAPÁ LEAD TSX LISTINGS SURGE — $4,000 Gold Restores Investor Appetite for Pre-Production Names
snippet: Mining.com reports that gold miners Cadillac Mining and Amapá Minerals are part of a growing wave of TSX listings that signal a meaningful recovery in Canada's junior mining IPO market, driven by gold's sustained performance above $4,000 per ounce and improved institutional appetite for early-stage production stories. The rebound reverses a two-year IPO drought during which sub-$2,000 gold made new equity raises structurally unattractive; the combination of a strong gold price, widening producer margins, and high-profile drill results from active exploration regions (Yukon, BC, Abitibi) has rebuilt the pipeline of companies willing to incur the costs and scrutiny of a TSX listing. For retail investors who track the junior mining ecosystem, a recovering IPO market is a leading indicator that capital is rotating back into the sector broadly.
